<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **3** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/kernel/contracts/index.mdx`  _(via IAIService (symbol, a top-level interface))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via IAIService (symbol, a top-level interface))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **173** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e71ecc1b32cca6a8c56ae1d949c0b9100465475e` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `591a5b74d787473417152b3d9eab376bbea34d30` — the merge of head `9a9adad009b29127e6f551fc959a06adedf0fdf0` into base `e71ecc1b32cca6a8c56ae1d949c0b9100465475e`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 591a5b74d787473417152b3d9eab376bbea34d30 && git checkout 591a5b74d787473417152b3d9eab376bbea34d30
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin e71ecc1b32cca6a8c56ae1d949c0b9100465475e 9a9adad009b29127e6f551fc959a06adedf0fdf0 && git checkout -B drift-repro e71ecc1b32cca6a8c56ae1d949c0b9100465475e && git merge --no-ff 9a9adad009b29127e6f551fc959a06adedf0fdf0

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e71ecc1b32cca6a8c56ae1d949c0b9100465475e
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs e71ecc1b32cca6a8c56ae1d949c0b9100465475e` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `10b5d04babce3a274793983aa868c14fc00db455`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/contracts/ai-service.ts + packages/spec/src/contracts/action-confirmation-contract.pin.test.ts, packages/spec/src/contracts/ai-service.test.ts

Inputs read: card #33808 (body and all four comments), ruling record 6893484458 on #33689, PR #34001 (body, file list, net diff against `main`), the check-runs on this head. Code read, not reviewed: `docs/adr/0011-actions-as-ai-tools.md` (invocation flow, confirmation table, amendment note), `skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md` :150-166, `packages/client/src/index.ts` :7707-7765, `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs`, `.changeset/33689-ai-action-confirmation-elicited.md`, AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist item 3. The service-ai approve and reject routes are not in this repository (cloud, #33809), so the first consumer was judged from ADR-0011 and the client SDK.

Check-runs at reading time. Completed, success: Check Changeset, Check PR Size, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests, PR-body guards, Spec property liveness, Dogfood Regression Gate, Flag docs affected by code changes, Auto Label, filter, Plan Test Core shards, Plan Test UI shards. STILL IN PROGRESS, so no verdict from them: Build Core, Build UI Deps, Test Core 1/8 to 8/8 (the shards that run the two pin files), Type Check (workspace, source gates, consumer gates, debt ledger), Lint · ESLint, Lint · docs & code guards, Lint · repo & tooling gates, Lint · CI, release & engine gates (carries the ADR-0087 registration gate), Lint · scoped · query-options erasure, Lint · scoped · slot lookup & corpus, Live E2E UI. No failed run. The rest are skipped.

### ① Derived judgments

- Public surface: no export, type, signature or schema moves. Right. The diff is TSDoc on `AI_ACTION_CONFIRMATION_CAPABILITY` and on three `IAIService` members, plus prose pins.
- Accept set, widening: none. Nothing a caller or an author can do today is newly admitted.
- Accept set, narrowing, stated by the contract for the implementing doors: (a) a holder of `ai:approve` no longer decides another user's item; (b) the approve and reject doors refuse an API key, a token, any service credential and an AI identity; (c) an approved item runs as the person with every gate re-checked, not through the pre-registered dispatcher; (d) rule 1 reaches the in-app assistant's action tools. Each is right against the ruling record (only the person the call ran as; a signed-in session only; runs as that person, permissions re-checked; the in-app card and inbox stay; a second approver goes through `held`).
- The narrowing is published by this diff as contract text and declared by it as bare `yes`. Wrong: see M1.
- No generated artifact moves. Right for TSDoc on interfaces and a constant; the `check:generated` verdict is in the unfinished Build and Test runs.

### ② Semver level

- Level: `@objectstack/spec` minor with `Metadata-protocol: semantic`. Right. The meaning of `ai.requiresConfirmation: true` changes for the in-app door (who confirms, and that the queue is its channel); a kind takes at least minor. Same level and kind as the #33689 changeset for the same contract.
- Clause-②: WRONG on this head. See M1.

M1 (must-fix) — the `Clause-②:` line under-declares a breaking narrowing. The PR body and the changeset both read `Clause-②: yes`. In the one reader (`scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs`) bare `yes` is "a widening", and this diff widens nothing. What it publishes is a narrowing, and the changeset says so itself: its sentence after the line names two refusals, and its last section is a FROM/TO migration for callers who are refused. The card asked for `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`; the seat's claim dropped the arm without a stated reason, and the PR copied the claim. The dev's ground for keeping it (nothing changes at a door in this release) was equally true of PR #33725 for #33689, which shipped the same kind of text in the same file under `yes (narrowing)`, with a `!` title, a BREAKING banner and an ADR-0087 marker. Two changesets on one contract cannot answer that question two ways. The arm is also load-bearing: the ADR-0087 registration gate keys on it, so without it the narrowing ships with no disposition and that gate has nothing to refuse. Deferring the declaration to "the implementing change" does not hold either: the deciding routes are in another repository (#33809), and `IAIService` is a contract a third-party host implements from the release that carries this text.
Fix: the seat re-claims with the `(narrowing)` arm, and the PR body and changeset carry the same line. `no (narrowing)` is the truthful spelling since nothing widens; the card's `yes (narrowing)` is also acceptable, as both read as breaking. The changeset then adds its ADR-0087 disposition marker and the BREAKING-when-implemented banner, as the #33689 changeset does, and the dogfood battery runs on the final head. The fix moves the head, so it earns a delta review.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev flag 1, `ProposePendingActionInput.proposedBy` stays optional: answered, option A. No shape change in this PR. By the letter of the new text an item with no recorded person is decidable by nobody (`actorId` is a required string and must equal `proposed_by`), so the gap fails closed; and rule 6, which rule 1 now applies to the in-app door as written, means a declared-gated call with no person behind it is not queued at all. The implementing card must refuse to queue without the person. The seat owes that sentence on the implementing card, which no input names by number; until it is written there this flag is only parked.
- Dev flag 2, bare `yes` against the card's `yes (narrowing)`: answered, option B. This is M1.
- Dev deviation, PR assignee unset: no contract effect; the seat's.
- Out-of-scope findings in the dev report (skills paragraph, client SDK docblock and docs page, ui decision hooks, cloud routes): correctly left out by the card's scope and named in the changeset's `Skills-docs:` line. Not reviewed.
- Security line: n/a, no `hits` path is under `skills/**` or `ui/skills/**`. The change is a permission boundary by the triage's own word; the label is the seat's call.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/contracts/ai-service.ts`, against the ruling record, ADR-0011 and the first consumer.

Holds:
- Rule 1 now names the in-app assistant's action tools beside the two MCP tools, keeps the DECLARED predicate, and says which rules are channel (2 to 4, MCP) and which bind every door (5 and 6). That is the ruling's "same rule, two flows".
- The in-app section matches ADR-0011 as it stands: the handler enqueues and answers `pending_approval`; the card and inbox show the item; with the queue unwired a gated action is not registered as a tool (ADR table rows 2 and 3, SKILL.md :152-156). "Not offered when unwired" is today's behaviour, stated, not a new rule.
- The three points are the ruling's three, and mirror the hand-off sentence for sentence (rule 3 step 2 and rule 4's last paragraph): who decides, session only with the same refused set, runs as the person through the admitted sequence (`packages/runtime/src/action-dispatch.ts` :4) with a refusal recorded as `failed`, a state `PendingActionStatus` and the client SDK's approve docblock already carry.
- The second-approver path is the existing `held` outcome, whose docblock is unchanged and consistent.
- "Its bounds" keeps the two seams apart, as the ruling left them (#33806). "When it binds" states the in-app FROM half, and it matches ADR-0011's flow (operator approves, pre-registered bypass dispatcher) and the client SDK docblock (`ai:approve`).
- The three member docblocks agree with the section. Signatures are untouched.

Findings:

S1 (should-fix) — the scope of the three points is stated two ways. Rule 1 limits the contract to the DECLARED flag, "never the listing heuristic", and the in-app section sits under that rule. The member docblocks bind every item: `proposePendingAction` says it is used when the action is dangerous by the heuristic OR declares the flag, and that the three points bind "the item from the moment it is recorded"; `approvePendingAction` and `rejectPendingAction` require `actorId` to be `proposed_by` with no condition. The changeset also says "someone else's in-app pending action", every one. A row does not record why it was queued (`PendingActionRow` has no such field), so an implementer cannot apply the points to declared-gated items only. A reader of rule 1 alone concludes that a heuristic-queued delete stays decidable by an `ai:approve` holder; a reader of the member concludes it does not. At a permission boundary the contract has to pick. Fix: one sentence in the in-app section saying the three points bind every item in the in-app queue, whichever trigger queued it, because the queue has one decider rule; or restrict the members and add what tells the two kinds of row apart. The first is the reading the tapped option supports (the in-app card stays, an administrator's approval moves to `held`). If the seat reads the ruling record's "for a declared-gated action" as excluding heuristic-queued items, that is a question for the maintainer, not for the dev.

N1 (nit) — `approvePendingAction` says another user "is refused" and the row stays `pending`, but not how the refusal reaches the caller. The return type's `failed` means an approved item whose execution failed, so a refusal has to be a throw; the docblock could say so. `rejectPendingAction` likewise. Left to the implementing card.
N2 (nit) — the in-app section says nothing about an item whose person never answers or has left. With only that person able to reject, such an item stays `pending`. The hand-off text leaves lapse to the host in words; the in-app text could say the same. Follow-up.
N3 (nit) — the sentence the diff extends in `proposePendingAction` still lists "has `confirmText`" as a danger signal, where `skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md` :153 says `confirmText` is dialog copy and not a destructive signal. Older than this PR and outside the card. Follow-up.

`packages/spec/src/contracts/action-confirmation-contract.pin.test.ts` and `packages/spec/src/contracts/ai-service.test.ts`, as the enforcement of the prose.
- Read against the head text with comment gutters folded, every new pattern matches a sentence that is there, and each pins a sentence of the ruling: rule 1's reach with the MCP-only wording as a negative control, the section heading, not-offered-when-unwired, the three points, `held` for a second person, two seams, the in-app FROM half, and the three members with `listPendingActions` as the control that carries none of them. `memberDoc` anchors on the member's declaration, not on a `{@link}` mention, and checks that the docblock closes above it.
- The pins agree with the contract. They pin wording only, as their header says. Their run verdict is the Test Core shards, still in progress.
- The S1 fix adds a sentence a pin should follow.

The changeset and the PR body's prose are not reviewed beyond ② and the declaration lines.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `b091e451b9773e1777dfdf67676b55fd311152ca`
Local-runs: none
Scope: delta round over round 1 (record 6897177404, head `10b5d04b`, FAIL on M1 with S1 open). One commit, 10b5d04b..b091e451: `.changeset/33808-ai-door-confirmation-in-app.md`, `packages/spec/src/contracts/ai-service.ts`, `packages/spec/src/contracts/action-confirmation-contract.pin.test.ts`, `packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.in-app-pending-action-decided-by-person.ts` (new), and the PR title and body as they stand.

Read: round-1 record 6897177404 in full; the seat's corrected claim 6897186176 on card #33808 (`Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: semantic`) and the card's comment list; PR #34001 title, body, labels, file list and comment list as of this reading (`updated_at` 2026-11-15T16:39:37Z, draft); the delta commit's message and full patch; `ai-service.ts` at the head, the in-app section and rule 1; PR #33725 (title, declaration lines, file list); `.changeset/33689-ai-action-confirmation-elicited.md`; `packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.action-requires-confirmation-elicited.ts`; `packages/spec/src/migrations/types.ts` (`SemanticMigration`) and `migrations.test.ts` (how the directory is read); `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs` (arm grammar); `scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs` (marker grammar and breaking signals); AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist item 3 and the Tier S paragraph. Code read, not run. `packages/spec/src/contracts/ai-service.test.ts` is unchanged by the delta and was not re-read.

Check-runs on `b091e451` at reading time: 67 runs, all completed, none failed, cancelled or timed out. Success: Build Core, Build UI Deps, Test Core and its 8 shards, Test UI and its 16 shards, TypeScript Type Check and the four Type Check jobs (workspace, source gates, consumer gates, debt ledger), Type Check UI, Lint & Repo Gates and its jobs (ESLint, docs & code guards, repo & tooling gates, CI, release & engine gates, PM dispatch-gates, the three scoped jobs), Build & E2E UI, Live E2E UI, Dogfood Regression Gate, Check Changeset, Check PR Size, PR-body guards, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Spec property liveness, Flag docs affected by code changes, Auto Label, filter, both shard planners. Skipped: Lint UI, Temporal Conformance, Dogfood Verify CLI, UI Published Artifacts, the Dogfood Regression Gate shard matrix, Build Docs, Queue verdict, Borrowed queue verdict, Schedule gate, 18.x upgrade harness, Packed-tarball smoke. The job that carries the ADR-0087 registration gate is green on this head with the new marker and entry in the diff; the Test Core shards that run the pin files and `migrations.test.ts` are green.

### ① Derived judgments

- Public surface: still no export, type, signature or schema move. Right. The delta adds one TSDoc paragraph, three pin assertions, changeset prose and one semantic migration entry.
- Accept set: the delta changes no judgment of round 1. Nothing widens. The narrowing is the same four statements, now with its reach over the queue stated once (S1).
- The new file is a registry entry, not a contract shape: `packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/` is read by directory listing at build and in `migrations.test.ts`, so no index edit is owed and none is missing. It carries no `conversionIds` and no `relevance`, which matches its sibling `18.action-requires-confirmation-elicited.ts` and is right for a notice with no mechanical move.
- No generated artifact moves in the delta. Right: the registry is generated from the entry files at build and is not committed; the API-surface files do not move for TSDoc.
- The declaration now exists in three places that must agree: the claim, the changeset and the PR body. Two agree. The PR body does not: see M1.

### ② Semver level

- Level: `@objectstack/spec` minor with `Metadata-protocol: semantic`. Unchanged and right, as in round 1; the new entry is a `semantic` entry and takes no higher level.
- Clause-② in the changeset: `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, line-initial, the arm the first token in the parentheses, explanation after it. Well formed in `clause2-line.mjs` (`declared`, value `no`, arm `narrowing`), and it equals the claim 6897186176. Right.
- BREAKING carriers in the changeset: summary `feat(spec)!:`, the marker `<!-- adr-0087: registered in-app-pending-action-decided-by-person -->`, the banner "**BREAKING, when the implementing change ships**" naming who is affected, the ⚠ line that nothing changes at any door in this release, the sentence that the semantic entry carries the same notice, and the FROM/TO list. This is the #33689 changeset's structure line for line. The marker names exactly one id, the id equals the entry's `id` and the file's name stem, and the entry is added by this diff, so `registered` is the honest disposition. Right.
- Semantic entry: step 18, all four required fields present, kebab-case id, license header, header comment saying why it is a structured TODO and why it is written conditionally. `surface` names the declared flag and "every other action the in-app assistant queues for approval", which agrees with the S1 sentence. `replacement` leads with the timing (until the release whose changelog says the door enforces it), as the sibling entry does. Consistent with the prior narrowing entry on the same contract.
- Clause-② in the PR body, and the PR title: WRONG on this head. See M1.

M1 (must-fix, carried from round 1, fixed in the changeset only) — the PR body and title still carry the round-1 declaration. As read now:
- body line 5 is `Clause-②: yes`. The claim and the changeset say `no (narrowing)`. Round 1's fix was "the PR body and changeset carry the same line"; AGENTS.md checklist item 3 requires the declaration in both.
- the title is `feat(spec): the AI-door confirmation rule binds every AI door, the in-app assistant included`, with no `!`. PR #33725 is titled `feat(spec)!: …`, and this PR's own commit and changeset summary carry the `!`. The PR title is what the landed commit is named by.
- the body's Acceptance notes still say "the claim carries `yes`, copied here", which is no longer true of the claim.
- the body's last line still reads "Dogfood battery: n/a, no `!` in the title and no `(narrowing)` arm on the claim's Clause-② line". Both grounds are gone. Round 1 asked for the battery on the final head, as #33725 reported its own; the body reports none. On the head only the Dogfood Regression Gate summary job ran, and its shard matrix is skipped.
- the body's Verification block is headed "Head 10b5d04b", lists three touched pin files and 46 tests, and does not mention the new semantic entry, the S1 sentence or `migrations.test.ts`. The "What changes" list names the changeset as "both declaration lines, `Skills-docs:` follow-up, FROM/TO" with no marker, banner or entry.
Why it fails the PR and is not a nit: the body is the maintainer's reading surface and one of the two places the declaration is required. As it stands, the body tells the maintainer this change is a widening with no breaking treatment while the changeset in the same PR ships it as a BREAKING narrowing. That is the round-1 defect, moved from the changeset to the body.
Fix: edit the PR, no code change. Title to `feat(spec)!: …`. Body line to `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`. Rewrite the Acceptance note and the Dogfood line to the present facts, and run and report the dogfood battery on `b091e451` as #33725 did (or state in the body, by rule, why it is not owed). Bring the Verification block and the "What changes" list to this head, including the new entry. The head does not move, so the seat can re-read the title and body against this record; no further code review is needed unless a commit is pushed.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Round-1 dev flag 1 (`proposedBy` stays optional): unchanged by the delta. Still parked until the sentence is on the implementing card; the seat's.
- Round-1 dev flag 2 (bare `yes`): answered by the claim and the changeset; the PR body is M1.
- The seat's choice on S1 (every item, heuristic-queued included) is the first of the two fixes round 1 offered and the reading the tapped option supports. If the maintainer reads the ruling record's "declared-gated action" as excluding heuristic-queued items, the new paragraph and its pin are the place to change. Flagged, not blocking.
- Labels on the PR are `documentation, size/m, tests, tooling`. Whether a breaking or security label is owed is the seat's call; no contract effect.
- Security line: n/a, as in round 1; no path under `skills/**` or `ui/skills/**`.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/contracts/ai-service.ts`, the delta paragraph in "The in-app assistant door".

S1: FIXED. The section now says, directly after the three points: "The three points bind EVERY item in the in-app queue, whichever trigger queued it: an action declaring `ai.requiresConfirmation: true`, or one the destructive heuristic gates (ADR-0011's confirmation table). A pending row does not record why it was queued, and the queue has one decider rule; an administrator who is to approve as well does so through `held`, never by deciding the person's item." That is the sentence round 1 asked for, with its reason. It agrees with the three member docblocks (which already bound every item) and with the changeset's new bullet. It does not disturb rule 1: rule 1 keeps "(the DECLARED flag, never the listing heuristic; …)" for the refusal on the MCP doors, and the wider reach is stated as the queue's decider rule, not as a wider refusal predicate. The two statements are about different things and do not conflict.

Nothing new is wrong in the contract text. One observation, not a finding: with every item bound, "not offered when unwired" still speaks of a declared-gated action only, which is correct, since ADR-0011's table decides the heuristic rows and this section does not restate them.

`packages/spec/src/contracts/action-confirmation-contract.pin.test.ts`, the delta assertions.
- Two new patterns pin the S1 paragraph: the "bind EVERY item … whichever trigger queued it: an action declaring `ai.requiresConfirmation: true`, or one the destructive heuristic gates" sentence and the "A pending row does not record why it was queued, and the queue has one decider rule" reason. Read against the head text with the comment gutter folded, both match what is there.
- A control pins that rule 1 still carries "(the DECLARED flag, never the listing heuristic;", so the queue's reach cannot leak into the MCP predicate unnoticed. This is the right control for this change.
- Not pinned: the trailing clause about an administrator and `held` in the new paragraph. The `held` path is already pinned under point 1, so nothing is lost.
- The run verdict is the Test Core shards: green on this head.
